description:
## Question

How does each of the six target workloads (see "Choose the target workload set") get into the catalog to the verdict's evidence bar (see "What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?"): how the anchor package's Elixir version and NIF are brought in (Mix.install of the package, vendored copy, or a faithful port), how responsiveness (worst tick gap) is measured beside the NIF, how small/large sizes and the crossover are reported, and which build tickets are handed off to the catalog epic (defk-9p6) with which real technical blockers (bitwise ops, [f32], [i16]/[i32], wrapping arithmetic, bit output).

comments.text: Per 'State kept between kernel calls' (defk-dtw.9): confirm that ex_data_sketch's Rust NIF also copies the HLL register binary per call (expected, since BEAM binaries are immutable), so the small-size comparison is like for like.

Per 'What do narrow element types ([f32], [i16], [i32]) mean in a kernel?' (defk-dtw.13): the [f32] and [i16]/[i32] blocker is now the build ticket 'Add [i16], [i32] and [f32] element types' (defk-4ai).

Per 'Can a kernel produce variable-length bit output, and in what form?' (defk-dtw.14): Gorilla's bit-output blocker is [Add the bitstring accumulator](defk-cmr); its bit reinterpretation is Defk.Bits.f64_to_u64/1, to be built with the rest of Defk.Bits and u64 from defk-dtw.10 (no build ticket for those exists yet; hand it off here).

Resolution:
- Sizes: each workload declares its realistic size in its header before any numbers, from how the anchor package is really called; the workload verdict is measured there, the other size beside it (goes into the verdict's Method). Crossover: ~6-point geometric sweep, smallest size where defk >= 2x the optimised baseline or 'none'; never changes the verdict; skipped when a large run exceeds ~1 min.
- Responsiveness: the tick_gap method (one scheduler, 1 ms ticker, large size), max and p99 gap for Elixir, defk and NIF, as a shared helper.
- Agreement: Elixir, defk and NIF identical for masking, PCM, HLL, Gorilla, Levenshtein; cosine top-k identical indices with scores within a stated tolerance. Disagreement fails the script.
- Defk.Bench.report/1 grows native:, responsiveness:, realistic_size:, sweep:; the verdict snapshot is generated from run_all.exs output.
- Anchors via Mix.install with exact pins, no vendoring: bandit 1.12.5 + bandit_native 0.1.2, membrane_audio_mix_plugin 0.16.5, ex_data_sketch 0.10.3, vettore 0.3.5, ex_strsim 0.1.0, gorilla_stream 3.0.3. All installed on macOS arm64/OTP 29; all precompiled except Membrane's NativeAdder (built locally by bundlex).
- Per workload: masking vs stale bandit_native (age stated), defk as a primitive_ops_module; PCM reproduces ClipPreventingAdder (NativeAdder's job: scale-down with hold-back), renamed 'PCM mixing with clip prevention', compared via mix+flush; HLL at the backend layer (confirmed: the Rust NIF copies the registers twice per call, so the copy is like for like); cosine top-k with each index resident (vettore flat index, [f32]/Nx tensor in :persistent_term), hand-written Elixir baseline; Levenshtein vs ex_strsim per pair via Enum.map (fuzler is a different job, header note only); Gorilla full encode job vs encode_elixir, headers and CRC32 in Elixir.
- Baseline optimisation lives inside each workload ticket.
Tickets (children of the catalog epic defk-9p6): [Extend Defk.Bench.report/1 for target workloads](defk-9p6.10) blocks all six; [Target workload: batched Levenshtein vs ex_strsim](defk-9p6.11); [Target workload: WebSocket masking vs bandit_native](defk-9p6.12) (needs defk-w38); [Target workload: cosine top-k over f32 vs vettore and Nx](defk-9p6.13) and [Target workload: PCM mixing with clip prevention vs Membrane NativeAdder](defk-9p6.14) (need defk-4ai); [Target workload: HLL update_many vs ex_data_sketch](defk-9p6.15) (needs defk-wlu); [Target workload: Gorilla encoding vs gorilla_stream](defk-9p6.16) (needs defk-wlu, defk-cmr). New build ticket [Add u64, masked arithmetic and Defk.Bits](defk-wlu), blocked by defk-w38. Glossary: 'Anchor package', 'Realistic size'.
Facts gathered by a subagent; package sources and test scripts in the session scratchpad (throwaway).
